title: Dispatch: lifecycle design consolidation, batch E (attempt 2)
description:
Repair batch E for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8, from the Sol fourth pass, bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.8 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.8`; read S3, S4, S14, S19, S20, S22, S23, S24, S25, S26 in full; history in .8.1, .8.4, .8.6, .8.7). The combatant lifecycle class has survived several repair cycles because rules are spread across many writers and batch D's checker only REJECTS invalid results instead of PRODUCING valid ones (S3, S22: a required exhaustion-6 death is refused by the checker). Per the review policy, this batch is a design consolidation, not another per-path patch. Migration 0038 is authorized only if the ammunition ledger needs a durable identity column (S19).

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
D1. One pure transition function for combatants, e.g. `nextCombatantLifecycle(current, event, context)` in a new module state/combatantLifecycle.ts, returning the complete next lifecycle state (status, hp, counters, recovery block, schedule + settled, head facts) or a typed refusal. `current` includes death rules, exhaustion level, head count/mechanic, effective max. Events: damage {amount, critical, damageTypes}, heal {amount}, clampToEffectiveMax (non-damage), setStatus {status}, optIntoPlayerCharacterRules, deathSave {roll}, stabilize, knockout, suffocationDrop, suffocationBreathe, exhaustionChanged {newLevel}, headDied, headsRegrown {count, hpPerHead}, recoveryDue {roll-free; uses stored schedule}, admission {suppliedHp?, suppliedStatus?} (start_encounter / projection / promotion). Priority inside every transition: terminal causes first (exhaustion 6 → dead; zero heads → dead; already dead stays dead except the I8 monster-healing exception), then the event's own rules, then the I6 clamp (non-damage; a clamp never changes 'dead'). The function never produces a state that violates I1-I8; the existing assert stays as a backstop only. Every combatant writer (updateCombatant, death saves, stabilize, suffocation, clamp, adjust_exhaustion's combatant path, head settlement, begin_turn accumulator resets, start_encounter insert/admission, actor projection and promotion, recovery resolution, schedule transfer/invalidation) computes its result through this function and validates every row it writes (S26).
D2. Monster-rules ordinary death stays revivable by healing (pre-PR behaviour, the I8 exception): heal on a dead monster-rules combatant with no exhaustion-6/zero-head cause → alive with the healed HP (S23).
D3. Exhaustion: adjust_exhaustion computes the new level, then applies `exhaustionChanged` (character and combatant) as ONE transition: level 6 → dead (HP clamped to the new effective max without changing dead); level 4+ → non-damage clamp; then character death side effects (attunement end, concentration break 'dead') run once (S3, S22). Mirror the same ordering for characters in hpLifecycle (a combined character transition; never write the condition and validate before the death is applied).
D4. Stable recovery ownership (S4): there is exactly one owner of a pending schedule — the actor's current projection row (active projection, else last-inserted combat instance row, per the existing helper). Promotion into a durable actor COPIES lifecycle (incl. schedule) into combatLifecycle for continuity but does NOT clear or settle the source row's schedule while that row is still the current projection; only projecting the actor into a NEW encounter transfers the schedule to the new row and invalidates old rows. Repeated promotion never overwrites an owned schedule with an invalidated one. resolveCombatantRecoveries resolves the owner row and syncs the actor. 'settled' only ever means a resolved zero-regain recovery (D5).
D5. Settled stable state (S14): settled = 1 is valid only with status stable and an all-null schedule; any partial schedule (some fields null, some not) is invalid regardless of settled, in both the clock integrity check and the invariant. Unrelated writes to a settled creature preserve settled (temporary HP grants, zero-regain heals, exhaustion changes that keep the max at 0). A heal or exhaustion change that raises the effective max above 0 while settled re-arms a fresh 1d4-hour schedule and clears settled (this is the existing batch-D rearm, keep it) — for characters (hpLifecycle writeHpFields path) and combatants alike. temp HP at 0 HP does not wake or heal.
D6. Actor invariants regardless of combatLifecycle presence (S25): campaign_actor writes always enforce I1 (exhaustion 6 → dead) and I6 (HP <= effective max), whether or not the subtree exists. Exhaustion on a campaign actor through start_effect condition projections (activeEffects.ts) is refused with the same error that points to adjust_exhaustion (single owner), like add_condition / update_combatant addCondition.
D7. Resolver threading (S20): thread resolveRulesPack into combatantHeadCount, anyConditionImpliesIncapacitated/conditionImpliesIncapacitated and every profile/mechanic lookup reachable from set_surprised and adjust_exhaustion's combatant path. Regression with installLateAmbiguityAddon for an ordinary goblin COMBATANT observer, a hydra observer, and combatant exhaustion (both succeed with the resolver; genuine unavailability still fails with no writes).
D8. Ammunition identity (S19): the expenditure ledger stores the ammunition identity (name, pack_ref, variant_id, properties_json) at expenditure time (migration 0038 adding these columns to ammunition_expenditure, backfilled from the current expended row where present). Entitlement per identity = floor(sum of original quantities / 2); returned = min(entitlement, present pieces of that identity across ALL its expended rows); remaining present pieces destroyed; report entitlement/returned/destroyed/unavailable. Test first/last/all/partial destruction, odd/even, mixed identities.
D9. Proof (S24): replace the seeded random sequence with a STATE-AWARE scenario generator: from each current state it picks among the events valid-or-meaningfully-invalid for that state (so record_death_save runs on dying creatures, stabilize on dying, set_suffocation drop and breathe both occur, healing and damage both occur, exhaustion both up and down, close/reopen, promotion via a summoning effect with campaignActorId), asserts the tool's expected outcome (success vs refusal) for each call, keeps the previous state to check I8 transitions, checks complete I7 (no partial schedules), and checks actor/projection parity including schedule owner and pending head facts after every reopen and promotion. Assert minimum success counts per event class so a generator regression that stops reaching a class fails. Keep the step count modest (a few hundred).
Also: table-driven unit tests for nextCombatantLifecycle covering every event × {monster, PC} × {alive, dying, stable, dead} × terminal causes, asserting the full next state.

Map every finding (S3, S4, S14, S19, S20, S22, S23, S24, S25, S26) to its tests in your notes, and list every writer you routed through D1 with file:line.
acceptance_criteria: D1-D9 implemented; all listed findings repaired with the listed tests; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report mapping findings to tests and listing routed writers in bd notes; bead closed by the child.

Decisions implemented:
- D1: nextCombatantLifecycle is the pure complete-state transition/refusal boundary. Combatant event writers, admission, projection, promotion, schedule transfer/invalidation, head settlement and begin-turn resets persist its full result and assert final rows.
- D2: ordinary monster death revives on healing; exhaustion-six and zero-head death remain terminal.
- D3: character and combatant exhaustion condition, effective-max clamp and level-six death are applied as one transition. Character attunement/concentration side effects run once after the combined final state.
- D4: one current actor projection owns pending recovery. Promotion copies lifecycle without clearing the source schedule; new projection transfers it and invalidates historical rows; repeated promotion preserves the owner. Recovery resolves the owner and syncs the actor.
- D5: settled means stable with an all-null schedule. Partial schedules fail integrity checks regardless of settled. Unrelated writes preserve settled; a positive effective maximum re-arms recovery.
- D6: campaign-actor I1/I6 checks run with or without combatLifecycle. Engine-owned exhaustion condition projections are refused in favor of adjust_exhaustion.
- D7: the resolver is passed to surprise/head and incapacitation/profile lookup paths. The test covers ordinary goblin and hydra observers and combatant exhaustion with and without the installed resolver.
- D8: migration 0038 snapshots name, pack_ref, variant_id and properties_json and backfills from surviving expended rows. Recovery totals entitlement per immutable identity and caps returns by matching pieces still present.
- D9: the state-aware lifecycle sequence checks expected success/refusal, prior-state I8 transitions, complete I7 schedules, actor/projection/head parity after operations and reopen/promotion, plus minimum event-class success counts. The pure transition matrix covers all events, profiles, statuses and terminal causes with full-state expectations.

Review finding to permanent evidence:
- S3: packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts, “applies direct level-six death and the effective HP clamp in one combatant transition”; packages/core/test/combatantLifecycle.test.ts full-state event/profile/status/terminal-cause matrix.
- S4: packages/core/test/encounterCombatants.test.ts, “promotes stable recovery through a summoning effect and transfers its single owner”; the D9 sequence also checks recovery and actor/projection schedule parity across promotion/reopen.
- S14: packages/core/test/hpLifecycle.test.ts, “settles zero-maximum recovery and keeps later clock advances valid” and “rejects partial settled recovery schedules in writes and clock scans”; packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts, “settles and re-arms zero-maximum combatant recovery” and “rejects partial settled combatant schedules”; D9 checks I7 after every operation.
- S19: packages/core/test/ammunition.test.ts, “keeps mixed identity entitlements separate after rows disappear or mutate”, “tracks each physical split row once”, odd/even recovery cases, and snapshot assertions; migrationRunner.test.ts covers surviving-row backfill and missing-row null identity; migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts covers adoption.
- S20: packages/core/test/actionEconomy.test.ts, “threads the exact campaign resolver through goblin and hydra surprise observers and combatant exhaustion”; it asserts success with the resolver and rollback/unavailability without it.
- S22: packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts, “clamps at six and applies the character death transition” checks direct level-six HP clamp, death and one ended concentration event; packages/core/test/hpLifecycle.test.ts exercises the combined character writer; combatant counterpart is the S3 test.
- S23: packages/core/test/encounterCombatants.test.ts, “revives ordinary monster-rules death by healing but preserves terminal death causes”; packages/core/test/combatantLifecycle.test.ts also asserts I8 and the terminal-cause exceptions.
- S24: packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts, “generates state-aware lifecycle operations and checks outcomes, I8, I7, and projection parity”, with per-event minimum success counts.
- S25: packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts, “enforces actor exhaustion invariants without combatLifecycle and refuses condition projections”; checks both I1/I6 and rollback through the real condition-package effect path.
- S26: packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts, “routes begin_turn resets through lifecycle repair before committing”; packages/core/test/combatantLifecycle.test.ts supplies the event/state matrix.
